![](images/40/406033f059dc4438ea55d43d2bd00b3b79bb99365a2e4846c995f4a447acfd82.svg)
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system." :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is
![](images/be/bed2784d17ee63b805917b492052daa7ef079c1682bbc78468eb10f314a92b1f.svg)

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](images/91/91175ab97472067cd14ffff740bb3a98718436f1e94de7a4a6d7fdfb1b35b81f.svg)

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $z,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $z$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1-5y \\ y=y \\ z=3,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1-5y \\ y \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186115124 :question/problem "Given the system
![](images/0e/0e89fc57b6af2ddf2a71246dbadc7feb8425d1e1e0ab8f988e7e8ad97d22cff7.svg)
which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent

- The system has no solution

- The system is consistent independent" :question/worked-solution "To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is
![](images/3e/3e3e8adb0d6e13f7d3b4c3e450b25a789480ac53189ab92385174688e460b2cc.svg)

Using Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -4 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](images/41/4122fb4ef56aa99161b15bc25001ca728a6cf7dae36d5dac0aac9b03dc411685.svg)

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
2x -3y= 4
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement I is true." :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186115242 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-6deb5ca1-ae5b-5721-895d-6efa8ac5fdfb"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186115071 :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is

![](images/6f/6fa4508463b059ce8ef9a5cfa720de9463e41ecdbfb16f4460870bb6fce444bc.svg)

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & k & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & k+4 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

![](images/21/215ff061dc7584055bf607f48d0048cb6bde4dcb1ed028fbf4c3a4bd47d89c25.svg)

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=-4,$ then the second equation is $0=-5,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=-4.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-32425960-ceab-536a-8061-1f2469974e99" :question/id #uuid "32425960-ceab-536a-8061-1f2469974e99" :question/math-academy-id "q-32220" :question/problem "Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=2 \\  & y+2z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system." :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-z=2 \\  & y+2z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+z \\ y=-2z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the latter can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2+z \\ -2z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-40f01e87-54e2-5dd2-9850-20313302577b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "6deb5ca1-ae5b-5721-895d-6efa8ac5fdfb" :question/math-academy-id "q-131730" :question/problem "Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+2y=12 \\  & x+ky=4\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 12 \\ 1 & k & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 12 \\ 1 & k & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & 4 \\ 0 & 2-3k & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+ky=4 \\  & (2-3k)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=\frac{2}{3},$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $x+ky=4.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=\frac{2}{3}.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-26b28742-5ee2-597a-8428-7062724625e9"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-26b28742-5ee2-597a-8428-7062724625e9" :answer-field/id #uuid "26b28742-5ee2-597a-8428-7062724625e9" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-32810e7f-ad8d-5b1e-a7d2-839ff11f12a9" :answer-field/choices ["answer-5b0d5bd9-5c97-5445-afdc-58640864c07d" "answer-0e30254f-fef5-5030-ad74-62323657f390" "answer-0250b550-0b7c-5c05-b8f5-33da7345f93c" "answer-32810e7f-ad8d-5b1e-a7d2-839ff11f12a9" "answer-e23cbcca-7092-5855-aeeb-dd2de6061a27"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5b0d5bd9-5c97-5445-afdc-58640864c07d" :answer/id #uuid "5b0d5bd9-5c97-5445-afdc-58640864c07d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "k=-\frac{2}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0e30254f-fef5-5030-ad74-62323657f390" :answer/id #uuid "0e30254f-fef5-5030-ad74-62323657f390" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "k=0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0250b550-0b7c-5c05-b8f5-33da7345f93c" :answer/id #uuid "0250b550-0b7c-5c05-b8f5-33da7345f93c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "k=2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-32810e7f-ad8d-5b1e-a7d2-839ff11f12a9" :answer/id #uuid "32810e7f-ad8d-5b1e-a7d2-839ff11f12a9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "k=\frac{2}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e23cbcca-7092-5855-aeeb-dd2de6061a27" :answer/id #uuid "e23cbcca-7092-5855-aeeb-dd2de6061a27" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "k=\frac{3}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186116493 :tutorial/content "We can use Gaussian elimination to find the general solutions of systems with any number of equations and variables. For instance, consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1, \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

This system has the augmented matrix
![](images/8a/8a8452587098eed9b697c3999c356359b949429f29ce16af2c81cf728be9480e.svg)

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\, & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable $z.$ From the second equation, we get $y=-3z,$ and from the first equation, we obtain $x=1-4z.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-4z, \\ y=-3z, \\ z=z.\end{aligned}
$$

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-4z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186115479 :activity/expected-seconds 720.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

[{:db/id 17592186116120 :step/content {:db/id 17592186116493 :tutorial/content "We can use Gaussian elimination to find the general solutions of systems with any number of equations and variables. For instance, consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1, \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

This system has the augmented matrix

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\, & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable $z.$ From the second equation, we get $y=-3z,$ and from the first equation, we obtain $x=1-4z.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-4z, \\ y=-3z, \\ z=z.\end{aligned}
$$

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-4z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "3eff050b-e4ba-52e5-aa10-7bba2feef2fc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 3162 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "6022e9b9-60ab-5ac5-b16a-17583fa649c3" :step/math-academy-id 17213 :step/next {:db/id 17592186116121}} {:db/id 17592186116121 :step/content {:db/id 17592186115241 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186115070 :question/id #uuid "dc6dd9b4-de7f-52d0-8ff9-a7a7f7a9abd7" :question/math-academy-id "e-4711"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "2d81e3f1-d930-59ee-b439-2a3645aebb6c" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186048742}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186115751} {:db/id 17592186115830} {:db/id 17592186266111} {:db/id 17592186266112} {:db/id 17592186302108} {:db/id 17592186302193} {:db/id 17592186326924} {:db/id 17592186400625} {:db/id 17592186402009} {:db/id 17592186402756}] :knowledge-point/title "Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination"} :step/id #uuid "79bb6bd1-8c36-5f56-9575-8a1b8388eb57" :step/math-academy-id 17214 :step/next {:db/id 17592186116122}} {:db/id 17592186116122 :step/content {:db/id 17592186116494 :tutorial/content "Recall that a system of linear equations is called **consistent** if it has at least one solution. This course is divided into three main categories: linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and probability & statistics. The linear algebra section covers crucial machine learning fundamentals such as matrices, vector spaces, diagonalization, projections, singular value decomposition, and regression, as well as dimensionality reduction techniques such as principal component analysis. The multivariable calculus section develops the tools needed for optimization and learning algorithms, including vector and matrix calculus. Finally, the probability and statistics section covers random variables, point estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and confidence intervals.

Students then explore matrices in-depth. They study Gaussian elimination, solve systems of equations, learn about determinants and their properties, and compute inverse matrices. These tools form the computational backbone of many machine learning algorithms.
As part of this course, students perform a deep dive into vector spaces, exploring linear independence, subspaces, bases, dimension, rank, and nullity. They also study operations such as the Hadamard product, which appears naturally in element-wise computations in neural networks. Students generalize key concepts to abstract vector spaces and inner product spaces, and study orthogonality, projections, and the Gram–Schmidt process.
Students will learn how to find eigenvectors of a matrix, compute matrix diagonalizations, and extend these ideas to orthogonal diagonalization of symmetric matrices. These techniques underpin dimensionality reduction methods and are central to understanding the structure of data.
The course then develops key applications of linear algebra in machine learning. Students study singular value decomposition and its relationship to principal component analysis, and learn how these tools are used for dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, and identifying structure in high-dimensional datasets. Linear least-squares problems and regression techniques are also studied as foundational methods for fitting models to data.

Students also study optimization of multivariable functions, including critical points, second derivative tests, and constrained optimization using Lagrange multipliers. These techniques form the mathematical foundation of algorithms such as support vector machines and constrained optimization problems in machine learning.
Students work with standard multivariable surfaces to build intuition for loss surfaces, and study double integrals as a tool for understanding continuous probability distributions.
On the probability and statistics side, students study discrete and continuous random variables, including probability density functions, cumulative distribution functions, transformations, expectation, moments, variance, and Bayes' theorem. Important probability distributions are explored in detail.
Students extend their understanding to joint, marginal, and conditional distributions, as well as sums and products of random variables. Topics such as covariance, correlation, and multivariate normal distributions are introduced, which are essential in probabilistic modeling.
